works.name: m4Bookmaker
works.hero: You own what you can hold, file by file, on your own machine.
works.short_description: A desktop app that converts folders of MP3 (or other audio) files into clean, properly chaptered M4B audiobooks you own outright.
substantive_description: A small app with a large argument. m4Bookmaker exists because Audible's ecosystem treats audiobook ownership as a license rather than a possession — a contract that can be revoked, a format that will not move, a library that lives on someone else's server at someone else's discretion. The technical solution is small — rebuild the M4B yourself from MP3s — and the position is large: you own what you can hold, file by file, on your own machine. The full pipeline handles automatic chapter detection from filenames, an interactive visual chapter editor with a built-in audio player, batch queue processing, and automatic repair of common encoding problems, with a deliberate GUI-to-CLI symmetry that keeps it scriptable without sacrificing approachability. It was one of the first tools built under the Ho System — concept to signed, packaged, distributed product in 3.5 days — and the position it embodies is structural: every time a tool gets repossessed by its platform, a small piece of personal capacity dies, and m4Bookmaker is the refusal of that pattern, sized to one specific failure.
Python with PyQt5 and FFmpeg; shipped as a signed macOS app and a Windows installer, and distributed as a PyPI package.

relationships.note: One of the first Ho System builds: concept to signed, packaged, distributed product in 3.5 days.

works.headline: Paused 2026-10-15 by practitioner.

state.last: Three sequenced agent-task specs built as four stacked branches, none merged. `b156cae` #14 loudness normalization: `--normalize`/`--normalize-two-pass` + GUI checkbox, loudnorm at I=-18/TP=-2/LRA=11 (spoken-word, not broadcast); two-pass measures then applies with `linear=true`; off by default and the ffmpeg command is byte-identical when off. `ba95a33` #23 silence chapter detection: new `m4bmaker/silence.py`, `--detect-chapters` + Detect Chapters button, chapter starts where silence *ends*, first always 0.0, sub-30s boundaries dropped. `01cdbeb` #4 Audnexus ASIN lookup: new `m4bmaker/audnexus.py`, urllib only, consent-gated, default takes Audible's *names* onto locally detected boundaries so remote offsets are never used. `43d2da4` cover suggestion: side-by-side `CoverChoiceDialog` with pixel dimensions, plus the CLI cover URL that #4 was dropping on the floor. Verification across the arc: 1213 tests green (1020 baseline, +193), coverage 91%, black/flake8 clean, mypy clean on all new modules with `window.py` held at its 30-error / 12-E501 pre-existing baselines, emoji guard intact, no new dependency. PRs #24→#25→#26→#27, each stacked on the previous. **2026-10-13, two more stacked on top**, both raised from a Reddit user question: `40331e2` #29 (PR #30) edit-mode cover now saves — the edit save never passed a cover, ffmpeg's stream copy kept the old art; cover now written to `covr` via mutagen, not best-effort, written before the in-place replace so a failure leaves the file untouched. `a9fa875` #28 (PR #31) source-file chapter markers kept when merging, on by default (practitioner rule: never discard metadata unless done explicitly) — new `Chapter.file_offset`; pipeline totals, repair re-timing (now by source via the repair mapping, not by row), GUI seek and Insert Time all measure from the file's start; build-mode reorder/remove-file hidden whenever rows aren't one-per-file via `_rows_are_files()`, which also closes a #25 hole where those buttons stayed live after silence detection. 1251 tests, coverage 91%, mypy at baseline 31; real-ffmpeg round trips for both; CLI E2E merge of two chaptered M4Bs verified.
state.next: **Paused 2026-10-15 by practitioner.** Resume by working through `ho-process/1.2.0-dev-test-checklist.md` against `dist/m4bmaker-dev.app` (arm64, ad-hoc signed, built 2026-10-14 from `a9fa875` via a scratch copy of `m4bmaker.spec` renamed to m4bmaker-dev, bundle id `com.sageframe.m4bmaker.dev`; test media in `dist/dev-test-media/`; `scripts/build_macos.sh` wipes `dist/`, so rebuild if missing). Practitioner tests the whole arc on `feat/m4b-source-chapters` (it contains all six), then merge #24→#25→#26→#27→#30→#31 and bump to 1.2.0; add CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entries at the bump (none written on the branches). Nothing ships on merge: `.github/workflows/build.yml` fires only on `v*` tags.
state.holdup: **No human has seen any of the new GUI** — Normalize checkbox, Detect Chapters button, ASIN field, cover chooser, edit-mode cover save, embedded-chapter build mode. Each PR leads with an unverified checklist. Three substantive unknowns: (1) silence-detection defaults (-30dB/1.5s/30s) are validated only on synthetic tones, never on real narration with room tone and breaths; (2) the `--asin-use-timings` *accept* path has never fired on real audio — the live E2E correctly refused, so only the refusal branch is proven; (3) the consent dialog wording needs the practitioner's own read. **Pre-existing finding, not caused by this work:** this machine cannot verify TLS certs from Python (`CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED` against any https host), which means `updater.py`'s update check has been silently failing here — it swallows errors by design. If the PyInstaller bundle ships without a CA bundle, both the update check and the whole Audnexus feature are dead on users' machines; worth checking the build before 1.2.0. **Confirmed 2026-10-14:** the built .app contains no CA bundle (no `cacert.pem`); the venv is Homebrew Python, whose OpenSSL looks in `/opt/homebrew/etc/openssl@3/cert.pem`, so lookups work on this Mac and would fail on a Mac without Homebrew. Fix (bundle certifi and point urllib at it) planned as its own branch on top of the stack. Three spec bugs found and fixed forward rather than worked around, all documented in the PRs: #23's verification recipe used `concat:` on WAVs (silently produced a 5s file, not 19s) and its 5s tones conflict with the 30s minimum chapter length; #4's `reconcile_offsets` spread as max−min hit its own stop condition, rejecting a correct shift on the commonest real case (Audible's `brandIntroDurationMs` sits *inside* chapter 1) — now median absolute deviation. Known limitation from #28: whole-file reorder is unavailable for books with embedded chapters (would need file-group-aware moves). Corrected: #15/#16 "output marked Protected" are closed on GitHub, not open. window.py mypy/E501 debt untouched by design. Operational note: `gh`'s active account drifts and does not follow the repo — check `gh auth status` before any `gh` call.
